(a) Interagency Coordinating Council on Prematurity and Low Birthweight.—The Prematurity Research Expansion and Education for Mothers who deliver Infants Early Act is amended by striking section 5 (42 U.S.C. 247b–4g). 
    (b) Advisory Committee on Infant Mortality.—
        (1) Establishment.—The Secretary of Health and Human Services (referred to in this section as the “Secretary”) may establish an advisory committee known as the “Advisory Committee on Infant Mortality” (referred to in this section as the “Advisory Committee”). 
        (2) Duties.—The Advisory Committee shall provide advice and recommendations to the Secretary concerning the following activities:
            (A) Programs of the Department of Health and Human Services that are directed at reducing infant mortality and improving the health status of pregnant women and infants. 
            (B) Strategies to coordinate the various Federal programs and activities with State, local, and private programs and efforts that address factors that affect infant mortality. 
            (C) Implementation of the Healthy Start program under section 330H of the Public Health Service Act (42 U.S.C. 254c–8) and Healthy People 2020 infant mortality objectives. 
            (D) Strategies to reduce preterm birth rates through research, programs, and education.  
        (3) Plan for hhs preterm birth activities.—Not later than 1 year after the date of enactment of this section, the Advisory Committee (or an advisory committee in existence as of the date of enactment of this Act and designated by the Secretary) shall develop a plan for conducting and supporting research, education, and programs on preterm birth through the Department of Health and Human Services and shall periodically review and revise the plan, as appropriate. The plan shall—
            (A) examine research and educational activities that receive Federal funding in order to enable the plan to provide informed recommendations to reduce preterm birth and address racial and ethnic disparities in preterm birth rates; 
            (B) identify research gaps and opportunities to implement evidence-based strategies to reduce preterm birth rates among the programs and activities of the Department of Health and Human Services regarding preterm birth, including opportunities to minimize duplication; and 
            (C) reflect input from a broad range of scientists, patients, and advocacy groups, as appropriate.  
        (4) Membership.—The Secretary shall ensure that the membership of the Advisory Committee includes the following:
            (A) Representatives provided for in the original charter of the Advisory Committee. 
            (B) A representative of the National Center for Health Statistics.   
    (c) Patient Safety Studies and Report.—
        (1) In general.—The Secretary shall designate an appropriate agency within the Department of Health and Human Services to coordinate existing studies on hospital readmissions of preterm infants. 
        (2) Report to secretary and congress.—Not later than 1 year after the date of the enactment of this Act, the agency designated under paragraph (1) shall submit to the Secretary and to Congress a report containing the findings and recommendations resulting from the studies coordinated under such paragraph, including recommendations for hospital discharge and followup procedures designed to reduce rates of preventable hospital readmissions for preterm infants.

fable.w: The section authorizes an Advisory Committee on Infant Mortality to give advice and recommendations to the Secretary on HHS programs, and it requires the committee's preterm birth plan to reflect input from scientists, patients, and advocacy groups, who are outside the federal government. The tempting "No" reading is that the interagency council, the National Center for Health Statistics representative, and the report to Congress are all intra-government. That reading fails because the advisory committee and the required outside input bring non-federal parties into shaping HHS activities.
fable.s: reflect input from a broad range of scientists, patients, and advocacy groups, as appropriate.

qwen_block.w: The section establishes an Advisory Committee that is required to develop a plan reflecting input from a broad range of scientists, patients, and advocacy groups. These groups are outside the federal government, and their input is required for the development of the plan, which constitutes participation in the decision-making process. The mention of 'patients' and 'advocacy groups' confirms the involvement of non-federal entities.
qwen_block.s: (3) Plan for hhs preterm birth activities.—Not later than 1 year after the date of enactment of this section, the Advisory Committee (or an advisory committee in existence as of the date of enactment of this Act and designated by the Secretary) shall develop a plan for conducting and supporting research, education, and programs on preterm birth through the Department of Health and Human Services and shall periodically review and revise the plan, as appropriate. The plan shall— ... (C) reflect input from a broad range of scientists, patients, and advocacy groups, as appropriate.

opus.w: The section creates an Advisory Committee that gives the Secretary of HHS advice and recommendations on HHS programs. It also requires the committee's HHS preterm birth plan to reflect input from scientists, patients, and advocacy groups, who are outside the federal government. That brings outsiders into a federal decision. The opposite reading, that this is only federal coordination or reporting to Congress, fits subsection (c) but ignores the outside input required in subsection (b)(3)(C).
opus.s: (C) reflect input from a broad range of scientists, patients, and advocacy groups, as appropriate.
opus.b: The tempting wrong reading is "No": the committee could be mostly federal officials (the only named member is from the National Center for Health Statistics, a federal agency), and subsection (c) is just an internal study and a report to Congress. That reading doesn't hold. The plan the committee writes for HHS must "reflect input from a broad range of scientists, patients, and advocacy groups," and those are clearly people outside the federal government. The committee also advises the Secretary on HHS programs, much like the advisory boards in Examples 10 and 12.

qwen_chat.w: The section establishes an Advisory Committee, but the explicitly listed membership consists of federal representatives (from the original charter and the National Center for Health Statistics). While the committee's plan must reflect input from outside groups, the committee members themselves are not explicitly identified as non-federal participants. Therefore, this is intra-governmental coordination.
qwen_chat.s: (4) Membership.—The Secretary shall ensure that the membership of the Advisory Committee includes the following: (A) Representatives provided for in the original charter of the Advisory Committee. (B) A representative of the National Center for Health Statistics.
qwen_chat.b:
Temptation: It looks like participation because it establishes an "Advisory Committee" and mentions "input from a broad range of scientists, patients, and advocacy groups."
Resolution: The definition of participation requires that the federal government consult or coordinate with people *outside* the government. While the committee is called an "Advisory Committee," the text explicitly lists its membership as including "Representatives provided for in the original charter" and "A representative of the National Center for Health Statistics." The National Center for Health Statistics is a federal agency (inside the government). The "original charter" likely refers to existing federal officials or employees. Crucially, the text does *not* explicitly state that the committee includes non-federal members (like private citizens, state officials, or independent experts) in its membership section. The mention of "input from... patients and advocacy groups" in subsection (3)(C) refers to the *content* of the plan the committee develops, not necessarily the *membership* of the committee itself. Without explicit language stating that non-federal individuals are members of the committee, we cannot assume they are. However, looking closer at standard statutory construction for "Advisory Committees" under the Federal Advisory Committee Act (FACA), they typically include non-federal members. But strictly based on the provided text, the membership listed is internal. Wait, let's re-read carefully. Subsection (b)(4) says "The Secretary shall ensure that the membership... includes... (A) Representatives provided for in the original charter... (B) A representative of the National Center for Health Statistics." It does *not* list non-federal members. The "input" in (3)(C) is for the *plan*, not the committee membership. Therefore, the committee appears to be composed of federal employees/officials. Thus, it is intra-governmental coordination.

Actually, let's look at the "Advisory Committee on Infant Mortality" in real life. It usually has non-federal members. But I must stick to the text. The text says "Representatives provided for in the original charter". If the original charter had non-federal members, they are included. But the text doesn't say that. It only explicitly lists federal representatives. The "input" clause is about the *plan*, not the *committee*. So, is it participation? The definition says "Participation is when the federal government may or must consult or coordinate with people outside of the government... Participation might happen in an advisory board... that includes non-federal members". If the text doesn't explicitly say the board includes non-federal members, and only lists federal ones, it's a "No".

However, often "Advisory Committee" implies outside input. But the prompt says "Be conservative... check WHO is involved." The only explicitly identified members are federal. The "input" is for the plan, not the decision-making body's composition. So, "No".

Wait, let's look at subsection (b)(2)(B): "Strategies to coordinate the various Federal programs and activities with State, local, and private programs..." This is a duty of the committee, but doesn't mean the committee *members* are from those groups.

Let's look at the "input" again: "(C) reflect input from a broad range of scientists, patients, and advocacy groups, as appropriate." This is a requirement for the *plan*, not the *committee*. The committee *develops* the plan. The committee itself might just be federal staff.

Therefore, the answer is No.
